sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: more suspension grounds, school-related loss for minors, surrender options, address records, reinstatement, speeding points, other point values, restricted license types, medical review, proof of financial responsibility, crash claims, crash-scene information and witnesses
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
The National Driver Register lists people whose licenses were canceled, denied, revoked or suspended, or who were convicted of certain serious traffic violations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Mental or physical conditions that interfere with safe driving, such as Alzheimer's disease, seizures or loss of consciousness, can lead to suspension or revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Perjury or giving false information about a vehicle's use or ownership or on a license application is grounds for losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
A felony involving a vehicle, evading arrest while driving, and manslaughter or vehicular homicide are all grounds for revocation or suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
Being a habitual recipient of moving violations, or not complying with a court judgment for crash damages, can lead to losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A01
Buying or possessing alcohol under age 21, or failing to meet child support requirements, can cost you your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A01
A driver found with five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle can have the license revoked or suspended. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A01
For the under-18 rule, dropping out means 10 days in a row or 15 total days of unexcused absence in a semester. [A01]
Why it matters: group minors and school; confusable dropping out versus unsatisfactory progress.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A01
For the under-18 rule, satisfactory school progress generally means passing three subjects each grading period. [A01]
Why it matters: group minors and school; confusable unsatisfactory progress versus dropping out.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A01
You can turn in a suspended license at any Tennessee Highway Patrol office or Driver License Service Center to get credit for returning it, or mail it to the department. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A02
Your new address may not appear on the card until a new, renewed or reinstated license is issued, but it must be correct on the official driver license file. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
Without a correct address on file you may miss important notices about your license status, and you could be ticketed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
Reinstatement steps depend on why you lost your license and what else is on your record, and the department's Financial Responsibility office handles clearing a record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A02
After a hearing, the department may try education, re-examination, license restrictions and probation to improve poor driving habits before turning to suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A03
Speeding 1 to 5 mph over the limit carries 1 point, or 2 points in a construction zone. [A03]
Why it matters: group speeding points; confusable regular versus construction zone.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A03
Speeding 6 to 15 mph over the limit carries 3 points, or 4 in a construction zone. [A03]
Why it matters: group speeding points; confusable regular versus construction zone.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A03
Speeding 16 to 25 mph over the limit carries 4 points, or 5 in a construction zone. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A03
Speeding 26 to 35 mph over carries 5 points, 36 to 45 mph over carries 6, and 46 mph or more over carries 8. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A03
Driving below the posted minimum speed or too fast for conditions carries 3 points each. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A03
Failing to yield the right of way carries 4 points, and improper passing carries 4 points. [A03]
Why it matters: group yielding points; confusable ordinary yield versus emergency vehicle yield.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A03
Following too closely, an improper turn, improper backing and failing to signal each carry 3 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A03
Reckless endangerment by vehicle, fleeing a law enforcement officer and child endangerment each carry 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A03
Driving when the required license is suspended, revoked or canceled carries 8 points, while driving without your license in your possession carries 2 points. [A03]
Why it matters: group license possession points; confusable under suspension versus not carried.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A03
Violating the restrictions printed on your license carries 6 points, and failing to report a crash carries 4 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A04
A driver convicted of DUI may get a court-ordered restricted license covering trips such as work, full-time college, worship, probation meetings, treatment programs and interlock appointments. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A04
After the first year of a two-year DUI revocation, a driver may apply for a restricted license by installing an ignition interlock for the rest of the revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A04
An adult suspended for frequent traffic violations may apply to the Driver Improvement Section for a restricted license, with an approval letter, SR-22 proof, tests and fees. [A04]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; confusable driver improvement versus court order.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A04
A person suspended by the court for implied consent, drag racing or a gas drive-off may ask the trial judge for a restricted license for work, full-time college and interlock appointments. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A04
A minor who loses a license over drug or alcohol charges may ask the trial judge for a restricted license to drive to and from school or work. [A04]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; confusable juvenile versus adult.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A04
A person suspended for an unsatisfied citation can get a certified court order allowing driving to and from work only, showing the fines paid or a payment plan. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A04
If a driver's medical report is unfavorable, the driving privilege stays suspended until the condition improves. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A04
The Financial Responsibility Law protects the public from financially irresponsible drivers and from drivers with repeated violations or obvious disregard for traffic laws. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A04
Accepted proof of financial responsibility includes your insurance policy declaration page or an insurance binder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R34 | anchor: A05
Proof of financial responsibility can also be an insurance card from a company authorized in Tennessee, a commissioner's certificate for a cash deposit or bond, or proof of self-insurance. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R35 | anchor: A05
If the driver cannot give the crash notice because of injury, a passenger who is able must make or arrange the notice. [A05]
Why it matters: group crash notice; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R36 | anchor: A05
If a crash involves an unattended vehicle or a domestic animal and you cannot find the owner, report it to the police. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R37 | anchor: A05
Owner/Driver Report forms are available on the Department of Safety website, at any Highway Patrol office, and at any local police station or sheriff's office. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R38 | anchor: A05
Not reporting a crash may lead to suspension of both your driving and registration privileges. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R39 | anchor: A05
When a claim against you is filed with the department, you must show you had liability insurance, get notarized releases from claimants, or post a cash or surety bond, or lose driving and registration privileges. [A05]
Why it matters: group crash claims; confusable three options.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R40 | anchor: A05
You may request an administrative hearing before a financial responsibility revocation if you ask in writing on or before its effective date. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R41 | anchor: A05
If your car is on fire after a crash, help the people out and move them away from the vehicle in case it explodes. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R42 | anchor: A05
Call 911 to report a crash as quickly as possible, and remain calm and stay at the scene. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R43 | anchor: A05
Exchange names, addresses and license numbers with other drivers, and get plate numbers plus the names and addresses of anyone injured and of each witness. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R44 | anchor: A06
Also collect other vehicle owners' names, addresses and insurance policy numbers, and notify your own insurance company right away. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec13-R45 | anchor: A06
If you saw the crash happen, pull safely off the road, turn on your emergency flashers and tell the officer or trooper that you are a witness. [A06]
Why it matters: group crash scene; confusable witness versus passer-by.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec13-R46 | anchor: A06
Secondary crashes near a crash scene are caused by drivers slowing to gaze at it out of curiosity. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]
